questions: Does text from a user (query string, form field, request body, file) reach a database query, a shell command, HTML, a file path or eval without being passed as a parameter or escaped?
Are keys, passwords or tokens written into the code or committed in a file?
Can someone reach data or actions they shouldn't, for example a missing login or ownership check on a new route?
Is a security check turned off, such as HTTPS certificate checks or input validation?

hints.title: SQL built by pasting a value into the string
hints.why: If that value ever comes from a user, they can rewrite the query and read or delete data (SQL injection).
hints.fix: Pass the value as a query parameter, for example db.query('... WHERE title LIKE ?', [value]), instead of putting it inside the SQL text.
hints.comment: Could this use a query parameter instead of putting the value inside the SQL string? If the value can come from a user, this allows SQL injection.

hints.title: Key or password written into the code
hints.why: Anyone who can read the repo, now or later in its history, can use it.
hints.fix: Move it to an environment variable (a .env file that git ignores), and replace the key, since it has already been shared.
hints.comment: This looks like a real key or password in the code. Could it move to an environment variable? It's also worth replacing the key, since it's now in the history.

hints.title: HTML built from a value
hints.why: If the value holds text a user typed, it can run their script in other people's browsers (XSS).
hints.fix: Use textContent for plain text, or escape the value before it goes into HTML.
hints.comment: Can user text end up in this HTML? If so, textContent (or escaping the value) would stop scripts running from it.

hints.title: Code run from a string
hints.why: Running a string as code means anyone who controls that string controls the program.
hints.fix: Replace it with normal code, or parse the data with JSON.parse or ast.literal_eval.
hints.comment: Is there a way to do this without eval? If any part of the string comes from outside, it can run arbitrary code.

hints.title: Shell command built from a value
hints.why: A value with characters like ; or && in it can run any other command on the server.
hints.fix: Pass the command and its arguments as a list (execFile, or subprocess.run([...]) without shell=True).
hints.comment: Could this pass the arguments as a list instead of building a shell string? A value containing ; or && could run other commands.

hints.title: HTTPS certificate check turned off
hints.why: Without the check, someone on the network can pretend to be the server and read or change the traffic.
hints.fix: Remove it, and fix the certificate problem it was working around.
hints.comment: Is turning off the certificate check needed here? Without it, the connection can be intercepted.

hints.title: Unsafe loading of saved data
hints.why: Loading pickle or full YAML from an untrusted source can run code hidden in the data.
hints.fix: Use json, or yaml.safe_load, for anything that comes from outside.
hints.comment: Where does this data come from? If it isn't fully trusted, json or yaml.safe_load would be safer.
